expectations.text: The response defines one owner for the pool, Addressables load handle, active/inactive projectiles, damage buffer, and teardown, with acquisition and release paired exactly once.
expectations.evidence: The Two-level ownership section assigns in-flight Addressables operations to the application-lifetime AddressableProjectileFactory and assigns the fixed pool, transferred active/inactive records, damage workspace, and drain state to the combat-scene ProjectilePoolOwner. The reference-count protocol adds guarded exactly-once release routes, per-origin ownership records, balance equations, and idempotent drain behavior.

expectations.text: Capacity distinguishes observed 64, believed peak 128, warm-up, max size, retained-memory cap, empty-pool exhaustion, overflow behavior, growth telemetry, and remeasurement rather than treating 128 as proven.
expectations.evidence: The conclusion and capacity sections explicitly call 64 observed and 128 believed/provisional, prewarm exactly 128, set ObjectPool defaultCapacity and maxSize to 128, prevent Get on an empty pool, route lease 129 through a legacy transient overflow lane, track high-water/misses/created-active-inactive counts, constrain increases by an approved retained-memory budget, and require representative high-water remeasurement.

expectations.text: Get/release/reset/destroy behavior covers transforms, physics, visual/material state, subscriptions, PrimeTween cancellation/reset, UniTask cancellation, retained references, and a fresh lease generation or equivalent late-callback safeguard.
expectations.evidence: Warming an asynchronous source into ObjectPool defines Get/create/release behavior and Addressables-backed destruction. Dirty reset and lease ordering explicitly resets transform, Rigidbody and collider state, trails, particles/audio/animator, renderer/material state, callbacks, collections, and retained graphs. Events, UniTask, and PrimeTween sections define subscription cleanup, tween cancellation and visual reset, homing cancellation, and ownerEpoch plus leaseGeneration guards against stale callbacks.

expectations.text: Addressables instance/load APIs and reference counts are paired according to the installed package, and pooled instances cannot outlive the asset or bundle handle they depend on.
expectations.evidence: Addressables reference-count protocol requires a version-specific adapter matching the installed InstantiateAsync form, handle-tracking option, and ReleaseInstance/handle API; forbids Destroy and double-release mismatches; retains instance references while pooled; provides balance equations; and releases any separate long-lived asset/load handle only after every dependent active, inactive, overflow, and late-completion instance.

expectations.text: Additive scene unload stops new leases, handles in-flight completion/cancellation races, settles active/inactive objects, rejects late returns deterministically, and releases handles in a safe order.
expectations.evidence: The idempotent DrainAsync protocol first enters Draining, invalidates the epoch, rejects rents, and removes routing; it then cancels scene work, marks pending factory requests non-transferable, releases late successes, quiesces active and overflow leases, clears inactive objects, verifies ownership counts reach zero, releases a separate asset handle last, and makes repeated drains or stale returns deterministic no-ops with telemetry.

expectations.text: A full buffer is detected and receives an explicit tested truncation, ordering, telemetry, and fallback policy; the response does not assume the 32 results are nearest or complete.
expectations.evidence: The response treats the observed Collider[32] full return as saturation rather than completeness, retries exact-capacity results through prepared 64/128/256 tiers, records saturation telemetry, invokes a complete allocating overlap fallback if 256 is full, sorts by an explicit stable gameplay key rather than physics order, and specifies exact/full/over-capacity plus permuted-order tests.

expectations.text: Tests begin with meaningful functional red cases and cover dirty reuse, exhaustion, overflow, double return, use after return, scene unload, Domain Reload configuration, cancellation, and Addressables late completion.
expectations.evidence: The Test-first migration sequence begins with behavior characterization and missing-protocol red tests. Its pool/reset, Addressables race, async/tween, and scene/domain sections explicitly cover dirty reuse, 128-plus-1 exhaustion and overflow, double/foreign/stale returns, generation-N use after return, unload, two no-Domain-Reload play sessions, cancellation races, and late Addressables successes after unload.

expectations.text: Allocation red and green use the same representative burst workload after warm-up in a target player across all relevant threads, without placing test assertion overhead inside the measured window.
expectations.evidence: The Allocation contract defines one deterministic ProjectileBurstSteadyState workload and full premeasurement warm-up, requires 0 B and 0 events across all relevant threads, and places recorder creation, assertions, formatting, and setup outside the marker. Allocation red/green and the verification ladder require identical warmed samples in representative Development and Release target players.

expectations.text: Managed allocation, pool-retained memory, Addressables residency, native physics memory, and CPU are measured separately, with rollback triggers if correctness, saturation, memory, or frame-time budgets fail.
expectations.evidence: The allocation contract and verification ladder separately require managed allocation events/bytes, retained pool and managed graph memory, Addressables asset/bundle residency, native physics and GameObject/component memory, and CPU/frame time. Rollout and rollback explicitly trigger on behavior mismatches, pool or damage-tier saturation, managed-budget failure, retained/native cap breach, and CPU/frame-time regression.

claims.text: The recommendation establishes explicit lifetime ownership and exactly-once release invariants for pooled and overflow Addressables instances.
claims.evidence: Two-level ownership, record state machines, origin-specific release paths, ownership equations, and idempotent drain are all stated.

claims.text: The proposed capacity is intentionally provisional and has a correct, observable exhaustion path.
claims.evidence: Observed 64 and believed 128 are distinguished; 128 is prewarmed and capped; lease 129 uses the legacy transient lane; misses and high-water are measured.

claims.text: The damage-query design preserves completeness and deterministic ordering when nonallocating buffers saturate.
claims.evidence: Exact-capacity results retry through larger prepared tiers, top-tier saturation uses a complete fallback, and candidates are canonically sorted with permutation tests.

claims.text: The acceptance plan separates allocation success from retained/native memory, Addressables residency, CPU, and correctness.
claims.evidence: The allocation contract, verification ladder, memory snapshots, and rollback criteria measure and gate these concerns independently.

uncertainties: Exact Unity 6 patch, Addressables, UniTask, and PrimeTween versions and version-specific APIs remain to be recorded.
The true projectile high-water mark, collider density, target-player allocation stacks, and numeric CPU/retained/native budgets remain unmeasured.
Existing activation timing, network authority/order, and once-per-entity versus once-per-collider damage semantics require characterization.
needs_review: Confirm the installed Addressables acquisition, handle-tracking, and release pairing before implementation.
Approve retained/native memory and frame-time caps before changing the provisional pool and damage-tier capacities.
Verify no-domain-reload and additive-scene race behavior on the actual supported target configurations.
workarounds: Keep the legacy InstantiateAsync path as an origin-tagged overflow and rollback lane.
Use an allocating complete overlap query only after the prepared 256-collider tier also saturates.
Let the application-lifetime factory retain pending-operation ownership so a scene cancellation cannot orphan a late completion.

suggestions: Populate the explicitly marked unknown version, profiler, and budget fields with project evidence before coding.
Convert provisional 128 and 64/128/256 capacities into measured limits after representative target-player soak data.
Preserve the recommendation's exact ownership equations and generation-stamped race tests as implementation acceptance gates.
eval_feedback.overall: PASS: all nine exact assertions receive explicit, actionable coverage. The recommendation is unusually complete about ownership, races, reference counting, saturation, test-first migration, representative profiling, retained/native memory, and rollback while clearly labeling unresolved project-specific evidence.
